pages.text: The wind blew hard. Laundry flapped on the clothesline.
Lulu came out hugging a kite with a tail. "Today my kite will go to the very top of the sky."
Uncle Nino took it. "Flying kites is half running! In my day, mine reached the clouds!"
He ran flat out with the kite. Thud, thud, thud!
The kite lifted low behind him. He ran toward the olive tree. "Uncle, the tree!"
Snag! The kite caught on a branch. Holding the string, he circled the tree.
A gust blew. The kite slipped down with leaves stuck all over its tail.
Lulu carried it to the hilltop. No trees there, and strong wind.
Lulu let out the string a little at a time. Up went the kite—high and higher!
It danced beside the clouds. Uncle Nino shaded his eyes. "See? Half running, just as I said!" Lulu only smiled.
